newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia govt sees economy growing 4-5 pct a year.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia govt sees economy growing 4-5 pct a year.

text.p: Slovenia's economy should grow by between four and five percent a year throughout the present government's four-year term of office, Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Tuesday.
"We expect GDP growth of four to five percent each year of this mandate," he told a meeting of Slovenian diplomats.
Raising the nation's international competitiveness in order to cut unemployment was a central task for the month-old coalition government, he added.
Ecomomic growth slowed to 3.5 percent last year from 3.9 percent in 1995, while unemployment rose to 14.6 percent in January from 14.4 percent a year before.
Drnovsek predicted a gradual slowdown in inflation, which was running at 8.5 percent last month.
"In the second part of the mandate, inflation should approach West European levels," he said.
He added, however, that a hike in fuel prices this year limited the scope for significantly reducing inflation in 1997.
The government has said it is aiming for three percent annual inflation by 2001.
